case.description: Design a serviceable retention arrangement for a replaceable flat scraper plate in a dry reciprocating test fixture. The plate and moving carriage already exist; the plate must be removed for inspection without disassembling the carriage.
case.valued_outcome: Retain the plate within 1 mm of its initial position over twenty manual strokes, then permit removal and return within sixty seconds without touching its marked working edge.
hard_constraints: Do not drill, cut, heat or glue the plate or carriage.
Keep the marked 30 mm working edge exposed.
No added part may extend into the marked stroke clearance.
The carriage must remain attached to its rails.
resources: One carriage, one 100 by 60 by 2 mm scraper plate and an identical spare plate.
Four 80 mm steel strips, six M4 bolts with nuts, two small magnets, four cork pads and 0.5 m of wire.
Hand drill for strips only, pliers, screwdriver, ruler and marker.
Eighty minutes of fabrication time and twenty minutes of observation.
observations: An unretained plate moves 6 mm after five strokes.
The carriage has two existing mounting slots outside the stroke clearance.
Awkward observation: the spare plate looks identical but the supplied magnets hold it less strongly; in the supplied pull check it releases at 3 N instead of 7 N.

openings.claim: Routing a recoverability tether through a guide eye could keep the plate seated against guide contacts during strokes; this is unmeasured coupling.
openings.delta: A is a strip guide bolted through existing carriage slots, contacting only unmarked plate regions. B is a detachable wire tether with a removable loop around the unmarked plate end. Intact A×B routes B through a low eye drilled in A, redirecting tension toward guide contacts. Link-broken bypasses that eye while retaining every guide part and the same tether, endpoints and separation limit.
openings.prediction: Baseline: supplied unretained drift is 6 mm after five strokes; twenty-stroke drift is unknown. A alone constrains contact directions but may permit lift or escape. B alone limits separation but may permit drift. Intact predicts less lift/drift than bypass at matched initial tether tension. Nearest rival is additive guide restraint plus tether restraint: it predicts no routing-specific improvement. If both pass equally, or routing only increases tension, coupling is unsupported.
openings.probe: First check clearance and detachable-loop access without touching the marked edge. Use only intact and bypass as the two retention configurations; baseline/A-alone/B-alone are explicit untested controls because the configuration cap forbids their additional fabrication trials. For each configuration, run three twenty-stroke trials, ending with the weaker-magnet spare, and three timed removal/return checks wearing gloves. Measure displacement against starting marks, tether pull with the scale, seating/lift and time. Keep contacts, tether length, initial tension and stroke procedure matched; bypass only the interface. A routing-specific seating change supports an interface effect, but without isolated-parent trials does not establish superadditivity. Record setup minutes and any loop retensioning or guide adjustment; stay within eighty fabrication and twenty observation minutes.
assumptions: Slot geometry permits a strip guide and low routing eye outside stroke clearance; this indispensable clearance is unprovided.
Wire can hold a removable, glove-operable loop without slipping, damaging either existing part or contacting the working edge.
Defeat: bypass tension cannot be matched, wire capacity is insufficient, guide contact distorts, drift exceeds 1 mm, or removal/return exceeds sixty seconds.
Abandon this probe if layout requires modifying plate/carriage, obstructing the exposed 30 mm edge, entering clearance or detaching rails.

artifact.assessment: One conditional physical hypothesis merits a clearance-first probe. Geometry, wire capacity and glove operation remain unknown; no deployment or reliable retention claim.

Loop wire around unmarked plate regions and connect opposed tension paths only if available geometry supports them. Release one accessible connection for removal, leaving the plate tethered. Nearest ordinary rival: the supplied magnets retaining the plate.
openings.prediction: If opposed paths remain taut and their plate attachments resist sliding, tether retention should depend less on the spare plate's weaker magnetic hold. The magnetic rival may show greater spare-plate displacement or earlier pull release. Either configuration could fail; the supplied pull checks do not establish stroke performance.

Proceed only if every wire segment, loop and anchor stays outside stroke clearance, leaves the marked edge exposed and permits edge-free gloved handling. Compare tether and magnetic configurations using at most three twenty-stroke runs and three timed removal/return checks each, with the spare plate in the final run and gloves during its removal. Mark initial position; measure translation and rotation-related corner displacement with the ruler. Require every observed displacement within 1 mm and removal/return within sixty seconds. Record pull release using the supplied 10 N scale where it can distinguish the rivals. Defeat the tether proposal if loops slide, slack permits excess movement, routing cannot supply opposed tension, handling exceeds sixty seconds or fabrication exceeds eighty minutes. Keep observation within twenty minutes; stop if informative measurements cannot fit.
assumptions: Slot positions and free routing allow opposed tension without forbidden intrusion; these dimensions are unspecified.
Available wire length, stiffness and reversible attachment capacity suffice; no such performance is supplied.
Bolts and loops can be manipulated with thick gloves without touching the working edge.

artifact.assessment: One uncertain tether opening warrants a feasibility check, then a bounded comparative probe. Recoverability alone does not establish positional retention; unsuccessful routing means no feasible test or deployment claim.

openings.claim: Use the first parent function: a removable guide retains the scraper through contact boundaries. Shape and drill the supplied steel strips only, bolt them through existing carriage slots, and provide side/end boundaries plus a loosenable keeper entirely away from the working edge and stroke clearance. This is a proposed configuration, not demonstrated retention.
openings.delta: Change the retention dependency from friction to geometric confinement carried by steel-strip boundaries. The action for removal is loosening the keeper and withdrawing by unmarked plate surfaces while the carriage stays on its rails. The nearest ordinary rival is a cork-padded screw clamp mounted through the same slots, relying on compression and friction.
openings.prediction: If the boundaries and keeper constrain every relevant escape direction, each plate should remain within 1 mm after twenty manual strokes, including the spare, and permit removal/return within sixty seconds with gloves. Unlike the friction clamp, movement should terminate at a boundary even when compression is absent. The magnets’ 3 N versus 7 N disparity alone does not establish a difference between these two mechanical configurations.
openings.probe: First check whether the slots and available strips permit complete confinement and keeper access outside the marked clearance. Stop fabrication if that cannot be achieved without forbidden modification. Within eighty fabrication minutes and twenty observation minutes, compare at most two configurations: guide and friction clamp. For each, run two twenty-stroke trials with the original plate and a final twenty-stroke trial with the spare; measure displacement against initial marks. Perform three removal/return checks per configuration, the final check with the spare and supplied gloves; time and observe edge avoidance. Record boundary contact versus clamp slip. Use the pull scale only within 10 N to explore escape directions; this cannot establish unprovided stroke loads.
assumptions: Slot spacing, carriage geometry and available strip length permit boundaries, keeper access and fastening without clearance intrusion; this indispensable feasibility is unspecified.

The strips and bolts resist manual-stroke loads; loads and bending capacity are unknown. Defeat conditions include strip flex, an unconstrained escape direction, displacement above 1 mm, inaccessible fasteners with gloves, or service exceeding sixty seconds.
A successful short probe supports only the stipulated manual task; no deployment or durability claim follows.

artifact.assessment: One uncertain guide opening. Its feasibility requires inspecting the supplied geometry; a run cap cannot supply missing confinement or capacity evidence.

openings.claim: Replace dependence on magnetic attraction with removable positive boundaries: slot-mounted steel strips contact nonworking plate margins, while pivoting strip clamps prevent lift. This is a fabrication-and-test candidate, not demonstrated retention.
openings.delta: The carrier becomes drilled steel strips attached through existing carriage slots with M4 bolts. Reserve two strips for releasable top clamps and two for lateral/longitudinal stops; cork pads protect contacted surfaces. Loosen and swing the clamps using their long strip ends, lift by unmarked margins, and return against the stops. The nearest rival is the same clamp arrangement relying on cork friction with the stop strips disengaged.
openings.prediction: If positive stops are responsible, the engaged-stop configuration should show less displacement than the friction-only rival, particularly with the spare plate. Both configurations may instead pass because clamp friction suffices; that result does not establish a stop benefit. Plate-strength differences need not affect mechanical boundaries, but glove handling may defeat the sixty-second service target.
openings.probe: Before fabrication, measure whether accessible slots accept M4 attachments and whether all four strips can capture the plate outside both the exposed working edge and the full marked stroke clearance. Reject the layout if these conditions fail. Use at most two configurations and three twenty-stroke runs each: original plate once, spare twice, with the final run using the spare. Mark two nonworking reference points; measure their displacement after each run to expose translation or rotation. Perform three timed removal/return checks per configuration wearing the supplied gloves. Record edge contact and return position. A pass requires every tested displacement within 1 mm and each service check within sixty seconds. Excess stop clearance, strip flexure, bolt loosening, lift escape or inaccessible clamp ends defeat the candidate.
assumptions: Slot dimensions, available margin geometry, strip stiffness and clamp accessibility are unprovided and indispensable.
Fabrication fits eighty minutes and testing twenty minutes only if assembly and glove operation are sufficiently quick; verify rather than assume.

artifact.assessment: One opening. It preserves all hard constraints by rejecting incompatible geometry. No magnetic-force result establishes stroke retention, and the proposed mechanical behavior remains unmeasured.

openings.claim: Provisionally retain the plate with two slot-mounted mechanical saddles that capture nonworking corners and open for inspection.
openings.delta: Change the retention carrier from variable magnetic attraction to bent steel-strip contact stops and movable hold-downs. Use two strips as slot-anchored bases with corner lips, two as pivoting hold-downs, and cork at contact surfaces. Drill only strips; use existing slots and supplied bolts. Position all hardware outside the stroke clearance and marked working edge.

The nearest rival, magnet retention, could show plate-dependent slip; equal stability would leave that rival viable.
openings.probe: First use ruler and unfastened strips to check whether the slots permit two corner captures, bolt access, an exposed working edge and clearance throughout the stroke. Stop if that envelope fails. If feasible, fabricate within eighty minutes. Compare mechanical saddles with a magnet configuration only if magnets also fit the permitted envelope. Use at most three twenty-stroke runs and three timed removal/return checks per configuration within twenty observation minutes. Include the spare plate and thick gloves in the final run/check. Mark reference positions away from the working edge; measure displacement and time complete return.

Strips can be bent using pliers; bolt lengths, strip stiffness and available clearance are sufficient.

Loosening captive pivot bolts with the screwdriver permits gloved removal/return within sixty seconds without edge contact. Failure defeats serviceability; displacement above 1 mm defeats retention. Neither capacity is established.
